The Master said: "My friends, what Yan says is right. What I said before was only a joke."
Gongshan Furao held the city of Bi in revolt and summoned the Master, who wanted to go. Zilu was displeased and said: "If there is nowhere to go, then there is nowhere; why must it be to Gongshan?" The Master said: "Would anyone summon me for nothing? If anyone were to use me, I would make an Eastern Zhou."
Zizhang asked Confucius about humaneness. Confucius said: "One who can practise five things in the world is humane." "May I ask what they are?" "Respectfulness, generosity, trustworthiness, diligence and kindness. If you are respectful you are not insulted; if generous, you win the multitude; if trustworthy, people rely on you; if diligent, you achieve results; if kind, you are able to employ people."
Bi Xi summoned the Master, who wanted to go. Zilu said: "Some time ago I heard you say, Master: 'A noble person does not enter the territory of one who does evil in person.' Bi Xi holds Zhongmou in revolt. How can you go?" The Master said: "Yes, I did say that. But is it not said that what is truly hard can be ground without wearing thin? Is it not said that what is truly white can be dyed without turning black? Am I a bitter gourd, to be hung up and never eaten?"
The Master said: "You, have you heard of the six sayings and the six obscurations?" He replied: "No." "Sit down, and I shall tell you. To love humaneness and not love learning - the obscuring is folly. To love knowledge and not love learning - the obscuring is aimlessness. To love trustworthiness and not love learning - the obscuring is harm. To love straightness and not love learning - the obscuring is harshness. To love courage and not love learning - the obscuring is disorder. To love firmness and not love learning - the obscuring is wildness."
The Master said: "My young friends, why does none of you study the Songs? The Songs can stir you, can help you observe, can help you live with others, can help you voice complaint. Near at hand they teach you to serve your father; far off, to serve your ruler. And you learn many names of birds, beasts, plants and trees."
The Master said to Boyu: "Have you studied the Zhounan and the Shaonan? A person who has not studied the Zhounan and the Shaonan is like someone standing with his face against a wall."
The Master said: "'Ritual, ritual,' they say - does it mean only jade and silk? 'Music, music,' they say - does it mean only bells and drums?"
The Master said: "One who is stern in look but weak within - to compare him with petty people, is he not like a thief who bores through walls?"
The Master said: "The respectable villager is the thief of virtue."
The Master said: "To hear something on the road and repeat it on the road is to throw virtue away."
The Master said: "Can one serve a ruler together with a base fellow? Before he has got what he wants, he worries about getting it. Once he has got it, he worries about losing it. And once he worries about losing it, there is nothing he will not do."
The Master said: "In ancient times the people had three faults; today perhaps even those are gone. The wildness of ancient times was free-spirited; the wildness of today is reckless. The pride of ancient times was upright; the pride of today is quarrelsome and perverse. The foolishness of ancient times was honest; the foolishness of today is mere deceit."
The Master said: "Clever words and an ingratiating look - there is little humaneness in them."
The Master said: "I hate the way purple takes the place of red, I hate the way the songs of Zheng corrupt the refined music, and I hate the way sharp tongues overturn states and families."
The Master said: "I would like not to speak." Zigong said: "If you do not speak, Master, what shall we your followers have to pass on?" The Master said: "What does Heaven say? The four seasons run their course and the hundred creatures are born. What does Heaven say?"
Ru Bei wanted to see Confucius, and Confucius excused himself on grounds of illness. When the messenger went out of the door, he took his zither and sang so that Ru Bei could hear it.
Zai Wo asked: "A three-year mourning period is already too long. If a noble person does not practise ritual for three years, ritual is sure to decay; if he does not play music for three years, music is sure to collapse. The old grain is gone and the new grain is ripe, the fire-drill wood has gone through its changes. One year is enough." The Master said: "To eat fine rice and wear brocade - would you feel at ease?" "I would." "If you feel at ease, then do it. When a noble person is in mourning, he finds no sweetness in fine food, no pleasure in music, no comfort at home; that is why he does not do so. But if you feel at ease, then do it." Zai Wo went out. The Master said: "Yu is inhumane! A child is three years old before it leaves its parents' arms. The three-year mourning period is the common mourning throughout the world. Did Yu not have three years of love from his parents?"
The Master said: "To eat one's fill all day and never use one's mind - it is hard to help such a person. Are there not gambling and chess? Even doing that is better than doing nothing."
Zilu asked: "Does the noble person value courage?" The Master said: "The noble person puts what is right first. A noble person with courage and no sense of right causes disorder. A petty person with courage and no sense of right becomes a robber."
Zigong asked: "Does the noble person also have things he hates?" The Master said: "He does. He hates those who proclaim the faults of others. He hates those who, being of low standing, slander their superiors. He hates those who are brave but lack ritual. He hates those who are bold and decisive but stubborn." He said: "Ci, do you also have things you hate?" "I hate those who take plagiarism for wisdom, those who take rudeness for courage, and those who take exposing others for honesty."
The Master said: "Women and petty people are the hardest to look after. If you are close to them, they become disrespectful; if you keep them at a distance, they resent it."
The Master said: "If at forty one is still disliked, that is how it will end."

keyLines.line: 性相近也，習相遠也
keyLines.en: By nature, people are close to one another; by habit, they come far apart.
keyLines.note: People's natures are similar; it is acquired habit that sets them far apart.

keyLines.line: 割雞焉用牛刀
keyLines.en: Why use an ox-cleaver to kill a chicken?
keyLines.note: Confucius came to Wucheng, heard strings and singing, and joked: why use an ox-knife to kill a chicken? Ziyou answered with 'the noble person who learns the Way loves people', and Confucius admitted it was a joke.

keyLines.line: 恭、寬、信、敏、惠
keyLines.en: Respect, generosity, good faith, diligence and kindness.
keyLines.note: Reply to Zizhang on humaneness: these five, practised in the world, make humaneness: reverence, generosity, trustworthiness, diligence and kindness.

keyLines.line: 不曰堅乎？磨而不磷。不曰白乎？涅而不緇
keyLines.en: Is it not said that the really hard can be ground and not worn thin? Is it not said that the really white can be dyed and not blackened?
keyLines.note: Confucius's answer to Zilu: what is truly hard does not wear thin when ground, and what is truly white does not turn black when dyed. With this confidence that he would not be tainted, he was willing to answer a summons.

keyLines.line: 好仁不好學，其蔽也愚
keyLines.en: To love humaneness without loving learning: the blindness in it is foolishness.
keyLines.note: The six sayings and six blindnesses: humaneness, wisdom, good faith, uprightness, courage and firmness, without a love of learning, turn into foolishness, aimlessness, harm, harshness, disorder and wildness.

keyLines.line: 《詩》可以興，可以觀，可以群，可以怨
keyLines.en: The Songs can rouse, can help one observe, can help one to be sociable, can help one to express grievance.
keyLines.note: Confucius on the use of the Songs: they can stir feeling, let you observe society, deepen company and give voice to complaint; close at hand they serve one's father, farther off one's ruler, and they teach the names of birds, beasts, plants and trees.

keyLines.line: 天何言哉？四時行焉，百物生焉
keyLines.en: Does Heaven speak? The four seasons run their course, and the hundred things are born.
keyLines.note: Confucius said he wanted not to speak; Zigong did not understand, and Confucius answered with Heaven as the example: what does Heaven say? The seasons go round and all things grow.

keyLines.line: 鄉原，德之賊也
keyLines.en: The village worthy is the thief of virtue.
keyLines.note: The agreeable good fellow who goes along with every current is a thief of morality.

glossary.note: Also called Yang Hu, a retainer of the Ji family in Lu who held power for a time.

glossary.en: shang zhi xia yu - 'the highest wise and the lowest foolish'
glossary.note: People of the very best and the very poorest natural endowment.
The same as 「鄉愿」: a person who seems upright but goes along with the crowd.
A gourd. Confucius did not wish to hang uneaten like a gourd, a figure for not being employed.

glossary.en: san nian zhi sang - 'three years of mourning'
glossary.note: Mourning for parents for three years; Zai Wo held that one year was enough.
A game of the chess type in the old days.

pian17.background: Several times in this book Confucius is inclined to answer a summons, from Yang Huo, Gongshan Furao and Bi Xi, which commentators have long discussed. Some think these passages show a conflict between Confucius's wish to save the world and reality.

pian18.summary: Book 18, 'Wei Zi', records the three humane men at the end of the Yin, Liuxia Hui, Confucius's leaving Qi for Lu, and recluses such as Jieyu, Changju and Jienni mocking Confucius. Confucius states his attitude of taking office to practise rightness, and the book lists the ranks of those who withdrew and the scattering of Lu's musicians.
pian18.translation:
The Viscount of Wei left him; the Viscount of Ji became his slave; Bi Gan remonstrated and was put to death. Confucius said: "The Yin had three humane men."
Liuxia Hui was chief judge and was dismissed three times. People said: "Sir, is it not time for you to leave?" He said: "If I serve people by the straight Way, where could I go that I would not be dismissed three times? If I served people by a crooked Way, why would I need to leave the land of my parents?"
Duke Jing of Qi, speaking of how to treat Confucius, said: "I cannot treat him as I would the Ji family. I will treat him at a level between the Ji and the Meng families." Later he said: "I am old; I cannot make use of him." Confucius left.
The people of Qi sent a gift of female musicians, and Ji Huanzi accepted them. For three days he did not hold court. Confucius left.
Jieyu, the madman of Chu, passed by Confucius, singing: "Phoenix! Phoenix! How your virtue has declined! What is past cannot be mended, but what is to come can still be pursued. Give up! Give up! Those who hold office today are in peril!" Confucius got down, wanting to speak with him, but he hurried away and avoided him, so Confucius could not speak with him.
Changju and Jieni were ploughing together. Confucius passed by and sent Zilu to ask where the ford was. Changju said: "Who is that holding the reins of the carriage?" Zilu said: "It is Kong Qiu." "The Kong Qiu of Lu?" "Yes." "Then he knows where the ford is." Zilu asked Jieni, who said: "Who are you?" "I am Zhong You." "Are you a follower of Kong Qiu of Lu?" He replied: "Yes." He said: "The flood sweeps on, and the whole world is like that. Who can change it? And instead of following a man who flees from people, would it not be better to follow those who flee from the world?" And he went on covering the seed without pause. Zilu went back and told the Master. The Master was saddened and said: "One cannot herd together with birds and beasts. If I do not belong with these people, with whom shall I belong? If the world had the Way, I would not be trying to change it."
Zilu was following behind and met an old man carrying a basket on a staff over his shoulder. Zilu asked: "Have you seen my Master?" The old man said: "You do not move your four limbs, you cannot tell the five grains apart - who is your Master?" He planted his staff in the ground and began to weed. Zilu stood with his hands folded in respect. The old man kept Zilu for the night, killed a chicken, cooked millet and fed him, and introduced his two sons. The next day Zilu went on and told the Master. The Master said: "He is a recluse." He sent Zilu back to see him, but when Zilu arrived he had gone. Zilu said: "Not to take office is wrong. The proper order between old and young cannot be set aside; how then can the duty between ruler and minister be set aside? He wants to keep himself clean and throws the great human relationships into disorder. A noble person takes office to carry out what is right. That the Way does not prevail, he already knows."
The men who withdrew from the world: Boyi, Shuqi, Yuzhong, Yiyi, Zhu Zhang, Liuxia Hui and Shaolian. The Master said: "Not to lower their aims or disgrace themselves - that was Boyi and Shuqi." Of Liuxia Hui and Shaolian he said: "They lowered their aims and disgraced themselves. Yet their words fitted the human order and their actions fitted careful thought, and that was all." Of Yuzhong and Yiyi he said: "They lived in seclusion and spoke freely; their persons were pure and their withdrawal suited the circumstances." "I am different from all of these: for me there is nothing that I must and nothing that I must not."
The Grand Music Master Zhi went to Qi. Gan, who led the second meal music, went to Chu. Liao, who led the third, went to Cai. Que, who led the fourth, went to Qin. The drummer Fangshu went to the region by the Yellow River. Wu, who shook the hand-drum, went to the Han river. The junior music master Yang and Xiang, who struck the chime stone, went to the sea.
The Duke of Zhou said to the Duke of Lu: "A noble person does not neglect his kin, and does not make his great ministers resent that they are not used. He does not discard old friends and followers unless they have done something grave, and he does not demand perfection from any one person."
The Zhou had eight scholars: Bo Da, Bo Kuo, Zhong Tu, Zhong Hu, Shu Ye, Shu Xia, Ji Sui, and Ji Gua.

keyLines.line: 殷有三仁焉
keyLines.en: Yin had three humane men.
keyLines.note: The Viscount of Wei left, the Viscount of Ji became a slave and Bi Gan died remonstrating; Confucius called them the three humane men of the Yin.

keyLines.line: 直道而事人，焉往而不三黜
keyLines.en: If I serve men by the straight way, where will I go and not be dismissed three times?
keyLines.note: Liuxia Hui was dismissed three times, and when told to leave he said: if you serve people with uprightness, where would you not be dismissed again and again?

keyLines.line: 鳳兮！鳳兮！何德之衰
keyLines.en: O phoenix, O phoenix, how your virtue has declined!
keyLines.note: The madman of Chu, Jieyu, passed Confucius singing, comparing him to a phoenix and mocking him for not withdrawing in a disordered age.

keyLines.line: 往者不可諫，來者猶可追
keyLines.en: What is past cannot be remedied; what is to come can still be pursued.
keyLines.note: The past cannot be mended; the future can still be caught up with. He urged Confucius to withdraw in time.

keyLines.line: 鳥獸不可與同群！吾非斯人之徒與而誰與
keyLines.en: One cannot herd with birds and beasts! If I am not with these people, then with whom?
keyLines.note: After Changju and Jienni spoke, Confucius said sadly: one cannot live among birds and beasts; if I am not with people, with whom shall I be?

keyLines.line: 天下有道，丘不與易也
keyLines.en: If the world had the Way, I would not be trying to change it.
keyLines.note: If the world followed the Way, I would not need to change it. It shows that Confucius travelled about because the world lacked the Way.

keyLines.line: 君子之仕也，行其義也。道之不行，已知之矣
keyLines.en: The noble person takes office to practise rightness. That the Way is not practised, we already know.
keyLines.note: Zilu's rebuke to the old recluse: the noble person serves in order to carry out rightness; that the Way will not be practised we have long known.

keyLines.line: 無可無不可
keyLines.en: No one thing I insist on, no one thing I refuse.
keyLines.note: After his account of those who withdrew, Confucius placed himself: I am different from them, with nothing I must do and nothing I must not do, depending on the time.

glossary.note: Removed from office three times.
Singing and dancing girls, whom Qi sent to the ruler of Lu to ruin his court.

glossary.en: chu kuang jie yu - 'Jieyu, the madman of Chu'
glossary.note: A recluse of Chu named Jieyu who pretended madness to avoid the world.

glossary.en: chang ju, jie ni - 'Changju and Jienni'
glossary.note: Two recluses who lived by ploughing.
People who lived in retirement and held no office.
Eight worthy scholars of the Zhou, born as four pairs of twins.

pian18.background: Most of this book consists of conversations between recluses and Confucius, reflecting the clash of the Confucian and Daoist attitudes to the world, and also shows Confucius's life choice of 'knowing it cannot be done and doing it'.

pian19.summary: Book 19, 'Zizhang', is made up wholly of sayings of Confucius's disciples: Zizhang, Zixia, Ziyou, Zengzi and Zigong on the scholar, learning, friendship and keeping the Way. Zigong also defends Confucius's standing, comparing him to the sun and moon, which cannot be surpassed.
pian19.translation:
Zizhang said: "A scholar who, faced with danger, is ready to give his life, who thinks of what is right when he sees a chance of gain, who thinks of reverence at sacrifices and of grief at mourning - such a man will do."
Zizhang said: "If someone holds to virtue without breadth and believes in the Way without firmness, how can he be counted as having it? How can he be counted as not having it?"
A disciple of Zixia asked Zizhang about friendship. Zizhang said: "What does Zixia say?" He replied: "Zixia says: 'Associate with those who are acceptable and keep away from those who are not.'" Zizhang said: "That differs from what I have heard. 'A noble person honours the worthy and tolerates the multitude; he commends the good and has sympathy for those who cannot.' If I am very worthy, whom could I not tolerate? If I am not worthy, others will keep away from me; how then could I keep away from others?"
Zixia said: "Even minor arts have something worth seeing in them, but when pursued far they may become a swamp, and so a noble person does not take them up."
Zixia said: "One who every day knows what he did not know before, and every month does not forget what he has been able to do, can be called a lover of learning."
Zixia said: "Learn broadly and hold firm to your purpose; ask earnestly and reflect on what is near at hand: humaneness is to be found in this."
Zixia said: "Craftsmen stay in their workshops to complete their work; the noble person learns to reach his Way."
Zixia said: "The petty person always dresses up his mistakes."
Zixia said: "The noble person has three aspects: seen from afar, he is stern; approached, he is warm; hearing his words, they are exact."
Zixia said: "A noble person gains the people's trust and then asks them to work; if he does not have their trust, they think he is oppressing them. He gains their trust and then remonstrates; if he does not have their trust, they think he is slandering them."
Zixia said: "In the great virtues, do not overstep the bounds; in the small virtues, one may come and go."
Ziyou said: "The disciples of Zixia are fine at sprinkling and sweeping, answering and replying, advancing and withdrawing. But these are only branches. When it comes to the root, they have nothing. What is to be done?" Zixia heard of this and said: "Ah! Yan You is mistaken. In the noble person's Way, what should be taught first? What should be left till later out of tiredness? It is like plants and trees, each sorted into its own kind. How could the noble person's Way be falsified? Who but a sage can carry it from beginning to end?"
Zixia said: "When an official has energy to spare, he studies; when a student has energy to spare, he takes office."
Ziyou said: "In mourning, express grief fully and then stop."
Ziyou said: "My friend Zhang does what is hard to do, but he is not yet humane."
Master Zeng said: "Zhang looks so imposing! It is hard to practise humaneness alongside him."
Master Zeng said: "I heard the Master say: 'People do not usually bring out their full feeling by themselves, but in mourning for their parents they surely do.'"
Master Zeng said: "I heard the Master say: 'In the filial piety of Meng Zhuangzi, the other things could be matched, but his not changing his father's ministers and his father's policies is hard to match.'"
The Meng family appointed Yang Fu as chief judge, and he asked Master Zeng for advice. Master Zeng said: "Those above have lost the Way, and the people have been scattered for a long time. If you find out the truth of a case, feel pity and sorrow for them, and do not take pleasure in it."
Zigong said: "Zhou's wickedness was not as great as it is said to be. That is why a noble person hates to be in the lowest place, where all the evil of the world flows towards him."
Zigong said: "The faults of a noble person are like an eclipse of the sun or moon. When he errs, everyone sees it; when he corrects himself, everyone looks up to him."
Gongsun Chao of Wei asked Zigong: "From whom did Zhongni learn?" Zigong said: "The Way of Kings Wen and Wu has not yet fallen to the ground; it is in people. The worthy remember its greater parts, and the unworthy remember its lesser parts. Everyone has something of the Way of Wen and Wu. From whom would the Master not learn? And why should he have a fixed teacher?"
Shusun Wushu said to the grandees at court: "Zigong is worthier than Zhongni." Zifu Jingbo told Zigong. Zigong said: "Let us compare it to the wall of a house. My wall comes up to the shoulder, and one can look over it and see the good things in the house. The Master's wall is many fathoms high. If you do not find the gate and go in, you cannot see the beauty of the ancestral temple or the richness of the many halls. Those who find the gate may be few. Is it not natural that the gentleman should say so?"
Shusun Wushu slandered Zhongni. Zigong said: "It is no use. Zhongni cannot be slandered. The worthiness of other people is like hills and mounds, which can still be climbed over. Zhongni is the sun and moon, which cannot be climbed over. Even if someone wants to cut himself off from them, what harm does it do to the sun and moon? It only shows that he does not know his own measure."
Chen Ziqin said to Zigong: "You are being modest. How could Zhongni be worthier than you?" Zigong said: "A noble person can be judged wise by one word, and judged unwise by one word; one must be careful what one says. The Master cannot be matched, just as the sky cannot be climbed by steps. Had the Master been given a state or a house, it would be what is called 'Establish them and they stand; lead them and they follow; bring them peace and they come; move them and they are in harmony. In life he is honoured; in death he is mourned.' How could anyone match him?"

keyLines.line: 士見危致命，見得思義，祭思敬，喪思哀
keyLines.en: A scholar who sees danger is ready to give his life, thinks of rightness when he sees gain, thinks of reverence at sacrifice and of grief in mourning.
keyLines.note: Zizhang on the scholar: in danger he gives his life, at gain he thinks of rightness, at sacrifice he thinks of reverence, and in mourning he thinks of grief.

keyLines.line: 日知其所亡，月無忘其所能，可謂好學也已矣
keyLines.en: One who daily learns what he lacks, and monthly does not forget what he can do, may be called a lover of learning.
keyLines.note: Zixia on love of learning: each day know something you did not, and each month do not lose what you already can.

keyLines.line: 博學而篤志，切問而近思，仁在其中矣
keyLines.en: Study widely and hold your purpose firm, ask earnestly and think of what is near, and humaneness lies within.
keyLines.note: Learn broadly and be firm in aim, ask keenly and reflect on what is near at hand, and humaneness is among these.

keyLines.line: 大德不踰閑，小德出入可也
keyLines.en: In great virtues do not overstep the line; in small virtues one may go in and out.
keyLines.note: Do not cross the limit in great matters; in small matters some freedom is permitted.

keyLines.line: 仕而優則學，學而優則仕
keyLines.en: One who holds office and has energy to spare should study; one who studies and has energy to spare should hold office.
keyLines.note: If you serve and have time left over, learn; if you learn and have time left over, serve.

keyLines.line: 君子之過也，如日月之食焉。過也，人皆見之；更也，人皆仰之
keyLines.en: The faults of the noble person are like eclipses of the sun and moon. When he errs, everyone sees; when he changes, everyone looks up to him.
keyLines.note: Zigong said: a noble person's mistakes are like an eclipse, seen by all when they happen, and all admire him when he corrects them.

keyLines.line: 夫子焉不學？而亦何常師之有
keyLines.en: Where did the Master not learn? And why should he have a regular teacher?
keyLines.note: Zigong's answer on where Zhongni learned: where did Confucius not learn, and why would he need a fixed teacher?

keyLines.line: 仲尼，日月也，無得而踰焉
keyLines.en: Zhongni is the sun and moon: there is no way to go beyond him.
keyLines.note: Zigong, answering Shusun Wushu's slander, said that other men's virtue is like a hill, which can be climbed over, but Confucius is the sun and moon and cannot be surpassed.

glossary.note: To offer up one's life.
Minor skills such as farming, gardening, medicine and divination.

glossary.en: sa sao ying dui jin tui - 'sweeping, answering, advancing and withdrawing'
glossary.note: Sprinkling and sweeping, answering guests and the etiquette of coming and going: the basic training of the elementary school in old times.
Several zhang. A 「仞」 is about seven or eight feet.
A grand master of Lu who slandered Confucius.
Chen Kang, a disciple of Confucius, courtesy name Ziqin.

pian19.background: This is the only book of the Analects that records mainly the words of disciples rather than of Confucius. It shows the different views among the disciples after his death, and their reverence for their teacher.

pian20.summary: Book 20, 'Yao yue', is the last book. It begins with the words of government handed down by Yao, Shun and Yu and the oaths of Tang and Wu, then records Confucius on taking office, 'honour the five fine things and put away the four bad ones', and ends with knowing fate, ritual and words.
pian20.translation:
Yao said: "Ah, you, Shun! The heavenly order of succession now rests on your person. Hold faithfully to the Mean. If the people within the four seas fall into hardship and want, the blessing of Heaven will end for ever." Shun also gave this charge to Yu.
Tang said: "I, the little child Lu (his personal name), venture to offer a black bull, and dare to announce to the Sovereign above, great Heaven: the guilty I dare not pardon. Your servants I do not hide; they are all examined in your heart. If I myself am guilty, let it not fall on the ten thousand regions; if the ten thousand regions are guilty, let the guilt rest on me alone."
The Zhou had great bounty, and the good were enriched by it. "Though there are those closest by blood, they are not equal to the humane. If the people have faults, let the blame rest on me alone."
He was careful with weights and measures, reviewed laws and regulations, restored abandoned offices, and the government of all quarters worked. He revived destroyed states, continued broken lines of descent, and raised up men who had withdrawn, and the people of the world turned their hearts to him. What he valued: the people, food, mourning and sacrifice. If you are generous you win the multitude; if trustworthy, the people rely on you; if diligent, you achieve results; if fair, people are glad.
Zizhang asked Confucius: "What must a person do to be fit for government?" The Master said: "Honour the five fine things and reject the four bad things, and he is fit for government." Zizhang said: "What are the five fine things?" The Master said: "The noble person is kind without spending, makes people work without resentment, desires without greed, is at ease without pride, and is dignified without fierceness." Zizhang said: "What does it mean to be kind without spending?" The Master said: "To benefit the people through what benefits them - is that not being kind without spending? To choose work they can do and ask them to do it - who will resent that? To desire humaneness and gain humaneness - what greed is there in that? The noble person, whether dealing with many or few, with great or small, never dares to be careless - is that not being at ease without pride? The noble person straightens his robe and cap and makes his gaze dignified, so that people look at him with awe - is that not being dignified without fierceness?" Zizhang said: "What are the four bad things?" The Master said: "To put people to death without having taught them is cruelty. To demand results without having given warning is tyranny. To be slack in issuing orders and then insist on a deadline is robbery. To be stingy in giving out what one must give anyway, as an official would be - this is petty officialdom."
The Master said: "Without understanding fate, one cannot be a noble person. Without understanding ritual, one cannot take a stand. Without understanding words, one cannot understand people."

keyLines.line: 天之曆數在爾躬，允執其中
keyLines.en: The succession ordained by Heaven rests on your person; hold faithfully to the mean.
keyLines.note: Yao said to Shun: the order of Heaven's mandate has fallen on you, so hold truly to the middle. 'Hold truly to the mean' became the heart-teaching handed down in the line of the Way.

keyLines.line: 朕躬有罪，無以萬方；萬方有罪，罪在朕躬
keyLines.en: If I have sinned, let it not touch the people; if the people have sinned, let the sin fall on me.
keyLines.note: From the prayer of Tang: the guilt is mine, so do not involve the people; if the people are guilty, the fault is all mine. It shows a ruler's responsibility.

keyLines.line: 興滅國，繼絕世，擧逸民，天下之民歸心焉
keyLines.en: Revive states that have been destroyed, continue lines that have been cut off, raise up those who withdrew, and the hearts of the people of the world will turn to you.
keyLines.note: Restore perished states, continue broken lines of descent and promote worthy recluses, and the hearts of all will turn to you.

keyLines.line: 所重：民、食、喪、祭
keyLines.en: What was stressed: the people, food, mourning and sacrifice.
keyLines.note: Four things government cares about: the people, grain, mourning rites and sacrifice.

keyLines.line: 尊五美，屏四惡
keyLines.en: Honour the five fine things and put away the four bad ones.
keyLines.note: The answer to Zizhang's question on taking part in government: respect five virtues and reject four bad practices.

keyLines.line: 君子惠而不費，勞而不怨，欲而不貪，泰而不驕，威而不猛
keyLines.en: The noble person is generous without waste, works the people without resentment, desires without greed, is at ease without pride, is awesome without fierceness.
keyLines.note: The five fine things: giving without waste, employing labour without breeding resentment, wanting without being greedy, being calm without pride, and being dignified without being fierce.

keyLines.line: 不教而殺謂之虐；不戒視成謂之暴；慢令致期謂之賊
keyLines.en: To kill without teaching is cruelty; to demand results without warning is tyranny; to be slack in orders and then set a deadline is robbery.
keyLines.note: Three of the four bad practices: killing without instruction is cruelty, expecting results without warning is oppression, and slack orders followed by a sudden deadline is robbery. The fourth, being stingy in paying out, is the way of a petty official.

keyLines.line: 不知命，無以為君子也；不知禮，無以立也；不知言，無以知人也
keyLines.en: Without knowing fate, one cannot be a noble person; without knowing ritual, one cannot stand; without knowing words, one cannot know people.
keyLines.note: The final chapter of the book: without understanding fate you cannot be a noble person; without understanding ritual you cannot take your stand; without judging words you cannot know people.

glossary.note: An exclamation used to call out to someone.
The order of Heaven's course, extended to the order of succession to the throne.

glossary.en: huang huang hou di - 'August Lord on High'
glossary.note: The great God of Heaven.
Balances and measuring vessels, meaning weights and measures.

glossary.en: wu mei si e - 'five fine things and four bad ones'
glossary.note: The five virtues and the four bad governing practices.
The mandate of Heaven; it can also be read as destiny or mission.
Originally the minor officials in charge of things. 「出納之吝，謂之有司」 means to be stingy when paying out what should be given, like a petty official, which shows no breadth of a noble person.

pian20.background: The first chapter has long been seen as the source of the line of transmission of the Way in Confucianism, linking Confucius's Way upward to Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen and Wu. The last chapter closes the book with 'know fate, know ritual, know words'. Some scholars think this book was added later.
